newsitem.title: USA: US debt fund managers on hold Sept 24 wk - survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt fund managers on hold Sept 24 wk - survey.

text.p: Money managers kept their U.S. debt portfolios largely unchanged in the week ended September 20, said a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
Portfolio strategists appeared to have been waiting until after the Federal Reserve's September 24 policy meeting to tinker with allocations, said a report on the survey.
"There simply was not much doing in the past week's survey," the report said. "(Respondents) were awaiting the Fed's response."
The report said the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading held steady at 4.00, while the asset-weighted number came in at 4.02, down from 4.18 in the previous period.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 7.18 percent from 7.21 percent.
Duration bogey held steady at 4.06 on an arithmetic basis and 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Twelve percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 4.0 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 4.00, unchanged from the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
